question: Which deity is worshipped during the Hindu festival, Chhath Puja?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Surya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chhath Puja is a significant Hindu festival dedicated to the worship of Lord Surya (the Sun God).
 
• Lord Surya is revered as the sustainer of life and the source of energy, light, and power in the universe.
 
• During Chhath Puja, devotees perform rituals and offer prayers to Lord Surya for the well-being, prosperity, and health of their family members.
 
• The festival involves a four-day-long observance that includes holy bathing, fasting, and offering prayers and prasad (sacred food) to the Sun God.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chhath Puja**

 
 
• Chhath Puja is celebrated mainly in the Indian states of Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, and in the Madhesh region of Nepal.
 
• The festival is observed in the month of Kartika, which usually falls in October or November.
 
• Chhath Puja is also known as Surya Shashti, as it is dedicated to Lord Surya and his consort Usha (the first light of dawn).
 
• Devotees believe that by observing Chhath Puja, they can cleanse their sins and gain blessings for longevity, prosperity, and happiness.
 
• The rituals of Chhath Puja include Nahay Khay (the first day of bathing and eating pure food), Lohanda and Kharna (the second day of fasting and preparing special offerings), Sandhya Arghya (the third day of offering prayers to the setting sun), and Usha Arghya (the fourth day of offering prayers to the rising sun).
 
 
 
• **Lord Surya**
 
 
• Lord Surya is one of the principal deities in Hinduism, symbolizing the Sun.
 
• He is often depicted riding a chariot pulled by seven horses, which represent the seven colors of the rainbow and the seven days of the week.
 
• In Hindu mythology, Surya is considered the son of sage Kashyapa and Aditi, and he is also associated with various other deities such as Agni (fire) and Indra (rain).
 
• Surya is worshipped daily by many Hindus during their morning prayers, and he is also celebrated during other festivals such as Makar Sankranti and Pongal.
 
 
 
• **Other Deities Mentioned**
 
 
• **Lord Krishna:** An incarnation of Vishnu, known for his role in the epic Mahabharata and his teachings in the Bhagavad Gita.
 
• **Lord Indra:** The king of gods and the deity of rain, thunder, and lightning in Hindu mythology.
 
• **Lord Ganesha:** The elephant-headed god of wisdom, prosperity, and remover of obstacles.
